q: The production of new organisms from the existing organisms of the same species is called reproduction.
e: This statement is true because reproduction is essential for the survival of species and ensures the continuation of life on earth.

q: Asexual reproduction in plants occurs through binary fission, budding, fragmentation, spore formation, and vegetative propagation.
e: This statement is true as it accurately lists the methods of asexual reproduction in plants.

q: A new individual produced from two parents is called asexual reproduction.
e: The correct term for a new individual produced from two parents is sexual reproduction.

q: Fission is a type of asexual reproduction that occurs in multicellular organisms only.
e: Fission is a type of asexual reproduction that occurs in unicellular organisms, such as cyanobacteria.

q: In budding, a small part of the body of the parent organism grows out as a bud which then detaches and becomes a new organism.
e: This statement is true as it describes the process of budding accurately.

q: Fragmentation is when the parent organism splits into two or more fragments, each fragment grows to form a new complete organism.
e: This statement is true as fragmentation is a method of asexual reproduction.

q: Spore formation involves the parent plant producing many microscopic reproductive units called seeds.
e: The correct term is spores, not seeds, as spores are the reproductive units produced during spore formation.

q: Vegetative propagation involves obtaining new plants from the parts of old plants without the help of any reproductive organ.
e: This statement is true as vegetative propagation is a method of asexual reproduction.

q: In artificial methods of vegetative propagation, new plants are obtained from seeds.
e: Artificial methods of vegetative propagation involve growing new plants from parts of existing plants, not from seeds.

q: Micropropagation is the process of growing many plants from one plant by man-made methods.
e: This statement is true as micropropagation refers to tissue culture techniques used to propagate plants.

q: Inheritance is the transmission of genetic information from generation to generation.
e: This statement is true as inheritance refers to how genetic traits are passed from parents to offspring.

q: Heredity is the passing of traits from offspring to parents.
e: The correct definition of heredity is the passing of traits from parents to offspring.

q: Chromosomes are organized packages of RNA found in the nucleus of the cell.
e: Chromosomes are organized packages of DNA, not RNA.

q: Each chromosome is made up of DNA and proteins and can be seen at the time of cell division.
e: This statement is true as chromosomes become visible during cell division.

q: A human body cell contains 46 pairs of chromosomes.
e: A human body cell contains 23 pairs of chromosomes, totaling 46.

q: Genes are segments of RNA that code for the person’s characteristics.
e: Genes are segments of DNA, not RNA.

q: The number of chromosomes is the same in all body cells of the same species.
e: This statement is true as all body cells of a species contain the same number of chromosomes.

q: Alleles are the alternative forms of a gene that occupy the same gene locus on homologous chromosomes.
e: This statement is true as alleles represent different versions of a gene.

q: DNA is the chemical substance found in the cytoplasm of a cell.
e: DNA is found in the nucleus of a cell, not in the cytoplasm.

q: The structure of DNA consists of two strands of nucleotides.
e: This statement is true as DNA is composed of two strands that form a double helix.

q: Mitosis is a process that creates two genetically identical daughter cells.
e: This statement is true as mitosis results in two identical daughter cells with the same genetic material as the parent cell.

q: Meiosis results in two diploid cells after two rounds of division.
e: Meiosis results in four haploid cells after two rounds of division.

q: Mitosis is important for cellular reproduction, growth, and repair.
e: This statement is true as mitosis plays a crucial role in growth and tissue repair.

q: Meiosis is a type of cell division that reduces the chromosome number by half.
e: This statement is true as meiosis produces haploid gametes from diploid cells.

q: The two stages of meiosis are called meiosis I and meiosis III.
e: The two stages of meiosis are meiosis I and meiosis II.

q: Mitosis occurs in all eukaryotic cells.
e: This statement is true as mitosis is a fundamental process in eukaryotic cell division.

q: The primary purpose of meiosis is to produce genetically identical cells.
e: The primary purpose of meiosis is to produce genetic variation through the formation of gametes.

q: Cellular reproduction is essential for growth and development in multicellular organisms.
e: This statement is true as cellular reproduction allows for the growth and maintenance of multicellular organisms.

q: Mitosis and meiosis are both types of asexual reproduction.
e: Mitosis is a type of asexual reproduction, while meiosis is a type of sexual reproduction.

q: Mitosis results in the formation of sex cells only.
e: Mitosis results in the formation of somatic cells, not sex cells; meiosis is responsible for forming sex cells.
